m: The {Magician} stands on the {Front Step} of the {Spa} and taps a giant *mouth* with his wand, and every plain statement it shouts gets a tiny *horse* galloping onto the end. "The bath is hot" turns into "The bath is hot, ma?" and the guests can only answer yes or no. The *horse* is a **question particle**, and the *mouth* now tacks that **question particle** onto everything it says.

The {Gardener} pops up through the {Trapdoor} of the {Hut} and refuses to hand over a single vegetable until you say the **measure word**: "one ge pumpkin, three ge carrots!" Whenever a *person* forgets, he slams a *pole* down in front of the noun like a turnstile. Soon the queue chants "ge, ge, ge!", because 个 is the all-purpose **measure word** that goes before almost any noun.

On the {Rooftop} above the {Piazza}, the {Juggler} tosses telescopes to a *standing person* in a long robe who yells "**Ga**!" every time he catches one. It is Galileo, 伽利略, and a glowing *plus sign* over his head adds that same **ga** sound to the front of his foreign name, so the crowd below chants "Ga-li-leo!" and spells it with 伽.

Down in the {Basement} of the {Spa}, the {Lifeguard} grabs a dented brass *trumpet*, jams it against his *mouth* and blasts "**La**-ba! **La**-ba!" so loudly the hot tubs bubble over. Towels flap, rubber ducks leap from the water, and the whole cellar honks back, because 喇 is the **la** in 喇叭, the trumpet.

In the flooded {Basement} beneath the {Lake}, the {Firefighter} rolls up a sleeve and his *tattoo* suddenly blazes with colour, so **brilliant** that the fish put on sunglasses. The inked *spread wings* peel off his arm, flap around the cellar and light it up like a stained-glass window: **brilliant** red, gold and blue, until the firefighter has to hose them down.

The {Yogi} drops through the {Trapdoor} of the {Spa} with a microphone and calls out every *woman* in the pool, adding a **ya** to each name: "Sonya! Tanya! Natalya!" Every one who answers gets a *silver medal* hung round her neck with a clang, because 娅 is the **ya** that ends girls' names when foreign names are written in Chinese.

On the {Rooftop} of a {Hut}, the {Yogi} cups a giant *ear* toward the *hillside*, where a choir of sheep sings "Ye-su, Ye-su!", the Chinese name of **Jesus**, 耶稣. The echo rolls back off the slope, the *ear* starts to glow like a halo, and the Yogi calls down to the village: "That 'ye' is the first sound of **Jesus**!"

The {Lifeguard} bursts onto the {Front Step} of the {Spa} with a megaphone *mouth* strapped to his face, and every sentence ends in a joyful "la!": "We're open la! Free towels la!" A *pulling hand* tugs passers-by inside by their sleeves while they cheer back with the same **excited particle**, until the whole street is bouncing to the **excited particle**.

On the {Rooftop} of the {Spa}, the {Ghost} floats along a row of sunbathers, bopping each one on the head and sticking an **A-** in front of their name: "Morning, A-Li! Hello, A-Mei!" An *auntie* in hair curlers waves a spatula in approval, because putting **A-** before a name is how she has called her nephews for fifty years: cosy, familiar and loud.

The {Hunter} tiptoes up the {Staircase} of the {Mansion} with a whole *clock* stuffed in his *mouth*, cheeks bulging and ticking, under orders to **hold in the mouth** whatever he must not swallow. At midnight the clock chimes and his teeth rattle, but he squeezes his lips shut, determined to **hold in the mouth** that clanging clock until he reaches the top step.
